props.name: icon
props.description: Flowbite Alert renders the status icon only when the icon prop is passed; the developed default (gate-shots *__default) shows none.

props.name: dismissable
props.description: Flowbite Alert renders the dismiss button only when onDismiss is provided; the developed default shows none.

rows.cause: CANVAS-DEVELOPED props. Flowbite renders the status icon only when `icon` is passed and the dismiss button only when `onDismiss` is, so neither prop is enumerable from the captured mount (captured-truth.json holds root → part-0 → label and nothing else). Until 2026-08-24 this fact was HAND-WRITTEN INTO THE CAPTURE RECORD (ac5e6181 back-porting c924c9c2's hand-edited contracts), so the record claimed a provenance no run reproduced and a fresh capture refused promotion by name — parity/receipts/v1/FIRST-PASS.md, selftest-tailwind 0/8.

rows.cause: CANVAS-DEVELOPED anatomy. The dismiss control mounts only when `onDismiss` is passed, so no captured plane carries the button, its themed background, or its radius. Until 2026-08-24 this fact was HAND-WRITTEN INTO THE CAPTURE RECORD (ac5e6181 back-porting c924c9c2's hand-edited contracts), so the record claimed a provenance no run reproduced and a fresh capture refused promotion by name — parity/receipts/v1/FIRST-PASS.md, selftest-tailwind 0/8.

description.from: Flowbite Alert renders the dismiss button only when onDismiss is provided; the developed default shows none.
description.to: When true, the dismiss control is shown. The click handler is the onDismiss event — not this boolean.

rows.cause: The seed bound the BOOLEAN `dismissable` to the `onDismiss` callback prop, so the authored React received a boolean where Flowbite expects a function and the dismiss control never clicked (NORTH-STAR functional gate, 968958cd). The boolean now binds to Flowbite's own `dismissable` prop; the callback moves to the declared `dismiss` event below. The capture reads DOM truth, not the React prop surface, so it cannot see this binding.

description.from: Flowbite dismiss control (onDismiss) — canvas-developed anatomy; close button with themed background per color.
description.to: Flowbite dismiss control — canvas-developed anatomy; close button with themed background per color.

rows.cause: The dismiss control is a real <button aria-label="Dismiss"> in Flowbite's DOM, and the declared `dismiss` event triggers on it — the authored React needs the element and the accessible name to be clickable and announced. The dismiss part is CANVAS-DEVELOPED anatomy (the captured default renders no dismiss button: Flowbite mounts it only when onDismiss is passed), so no capture plane carries the element or its attributes.

events.name: dismiss
events.description: Fires when the dismiss control is activated. The parent unmounts or hides the alert — the canvas cannot run this, so Figma shows the control as a boolean.

rows.cause: Declared event (core/emit-react.ts execute gate, 968958cd): the `onDismiss` callback is a code-surface fact with no canvas expression and no computed-style footprint — the capture drives prop combos and pseudo-class states, never a click handler. Placed after `anatomy` to keep the committed byte order.

fields.roleException: Flowbite ToggleSwitch is a <button role="switch">; the library has no native checkbox in the DOM.

rows.cause: Flowbite's ToggleSwitch renders <button role="switch"> with no native checkbox; the authored React must carry the ARIA role (and the named exception to the checkbox expectation) for the `toggle` event's aria-checked flip to be correct. The capture's semantics read is element-only; roles are not a computed style.

The flex root's cross-axis alignment (`align-items: center`, Flowbite's `items-center`) — the track and the label sit on one centre line. The capture lowered the root to `display: flex` and carried no align fact for it; the authored React clipped the label against the track without it (968958cd).

events.name: toggle
events.description: Fires when the switch is activated. Uncontrolled instances flip checked themselves — the canvas cannot run this, so Figma shows both values as variants.

rows.cause: Declared event (core/emit-react.ts execute gate, 968958cd): `onToggle` flips the `checked` variant axis and mirrors it to aria-checked — a code-surface fact the capture cannot see (it reads computed style per prop combo, never a click). Placed after `anatomy` to keep the committed byte order.
